_note: P13R: the approved P13 treatment, re-paced for a first viewing (STANDARD §3B) on a refined ~74 s narration (projects/charlab_p13r/story/script.json). Same worlds, metaphors, characters and transitions; each idea becomes one developing composition. Storyboard frames: the approved P13 key frames. Awaiting approval (gate closed).

thesis.understand: A family's mortgage was sold, pooled and turned into a security with ranked claims, so when families stopped paying the losses travelled from their kitchen to investors worldwide.
thesis.feel: The growing distance between the people who owe and the people who own, then the shock of the consequence coming home.

arc: intimate (a kitchen table) → abstract and distant (pool, security, world) → the mechanism breaks → home again, changed
through_line: One family's loan: their house is gold on every map, in the pool and under the building, and it is the first to turn red.

worlds.place: the family's kitchen in a street of similar houses, 2006 at dusk
worlds.role: the loan is signed; the stakes are a home

worlds.place: the town from above: four neighbourhoods, two local lenders, the pool
worlds.role: origination and pooling: thousands of loans become one pool

worlds.place: an architect's paper model of the security on a drafting table
worlds.role: issuance, the payment waterfall and loss allocation

worlds.place: the world map of the P12 library
worlds.role: distribution: each tranche sold to investors abroad

worlds.place: the same kitchen, September 2008, at night

motifs: warm pendant light (home, 2006) against cold street light (2008)
the ledger line: gold rules between tranches
signature: the gold thread of one family's loan

sequences.narration: In 2006, a family signs a mortgage on their first home. The monthly payment takes almost everything they earn.
sequences.understand: a real household takes on a loan that strains its income

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: a couple in a bank office, a form on the desk
concepts.why: P12 did this; the office tells us nothing about what is at stake

concepts.name: the kitchen table
concepts.idea: they sign at their own kitchen table at dusk; the street of similar houses through the window
concepts.why: the home is the stake, the street seeds the pool, and the table becomes the bookend

sequences.human_anchor: the family (husband and wife, P12 cast identities)

acting.does: leans in over the papers with his weight forward, the pen at his hand

acting.wants: to be sure they can pay
acting.does: holds her mug close and watches him, not the papers

sequences.staging: push in from the two-shot to the papers on 'barely afford'; insert: the payment line on the page against their income (cut on action: pen lifted, then the signed page)

transitions.motive: the camera drifts past them through the window to the street of houses

storyboard.shows: the kitchen two-shot at dusk; the mortgage on the table

steps: they sign at their kitchen table

sequences.narration: Their lender doesn't keep the loan. It sells it on. Lenders across the country do the same, and thousands of mortgages are gathered into a single pool.
sequences.understand: the lender's link to the loan ends; it is sold

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: a SOLD stamp on a folder
concepts.why: a stamp in a void shows a sale but not who sold to whom

concepts.name: the street rises into the map
concepts.idea: the papers seen from above dissolve into the town from above; their house gold; their loan runs to their lender, is sold on into the pool; the country's loans follow; one pool fills (one developing map)
concepts.why: the move from the street to the town itself says the loan is leaving home

accuracy: The lender originates and sells; it often still held some risk (warehouse lines, repurchase obligations), so the map must not show its link vanishing entirely: the sale line stays drawn.
sequences.human_anchor: their house, gold among the others

transitions.motive: match cut on shape: the filled pool becomes the plinth of the model

steps: the country's loans fill one pool

sequences.narration: On top of that pool, a new security is issued. In this simplified example, it has three layers, called tranches. Each month, the families' payments flow in. The top layer, the senior tranche, is paid first. The layers below are paid only after it.
sequences.understand: pooling and issuance are two steps: loans fill a pool (a trust), and a security with ranked tranches is issued on it

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.why: it merges pooling and issuance and hides the tranches, the key to what happens later

concepts.name: pool, then building
concepts.idea: the pool becomes the foundation of a paper-model building: a new security in three tranches (a simplified example); payments climb the servicer's pipe and are paid from the top down (one developing composition)
concepts.why: foundation and floors keep the two steps distinct and set up both the waterfall and the losses

accuracy: The pool is not the security: the foundation (loans) and the building (claims on them) are separate objects.
Tranches are claims with priority, not separate loans: every floor stands on the same pool.
sequences.human_anchor: their gold house in the foundation

transitions.motive: on 'around the world': from the building's roof out to the map, Wall Street at its centre

storyboard.shows: the town's loans converge into one pool; their loan in gold
the security as a building of three tranches on the pool

steps: senior first, then the layers below

sequences.narration: Pension funds, banks and insurers around the world buy these layers for their steady income.
sequences.understand: different investors own different floors, and payments flow to them by priority

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: a world map with routes to buyers (P12)
concepts.why: as P12 used it, it showed one product sold, not who owns which risk

concepts.name: floors sold abroad
concepts.idea: the world map: each buyer arrives on its word (pension fund, bank, insurer) with the layer it holds; steady payments flow to them (buyers illustrative)
concepts.why: shows the waterfall and that senior pieces went to cautious holders, so the later shock lands on them too

accuracy: Buyers, countries and tranches are illustrative patterns, labelled on screen.
sequences.human_anchor_reason: the investors are institutions; the line 'Every payment starts at a kitchen table' keeps the family present

transitions.motive: the routes' payment dots fade; the map zooms back down to the town

storyboard.shows: each floor sold to a different investor abroad

steps: buyers abroad, each on its word

sequences.narration: Then house prices fall. Families who can't keep up, and can't sell for enough to repay,
sequences.understand: the houses behind the loans lose value

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.why: correct but detached from the town we have been following

concepts.name: the chart grows out of the town
concepts.idea: back on the street map, FOR SALE signs appear; the national price index line (sourced, labelled) draws across the rooftops and turns down
concepts.why: the data stays tied to the place, and the line is the ledger line again

sequences.human_anchor: the street their house is on

transitions.motive: push in on their gold house; dissolve on its window to the kitchen at night

steps: FOR SALE: selling no longer repays

sequences.understand: the loans fail at the household level first

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: a wife with a coffee and an overdue notice in a borrowed office window set (P12)
concepts.why: the room was not their home, and the notice lay on the desk unread

concepts.name: the same table, two years later
concepts.idea: the kitchen at night, the pendant off, one lamp left on by the sink; she holds the letter; he has turned away
concepts.why: the bookend: same place, same people, changed light. The cost is shown in posture and hands

acting.wants: to understand what the letter means for the house
acting.does: holds the letter in both hands; on 'stop' her head drops to it

acting.wants: a way out he cannot find
acting.does: sits back, shoulders down, and turns his head away from the letter

transitions.motive: cut on 'bottom': from the family to the foundation of the building, where their house is

storyboard.shows: the same kitchen, 2008: the letter in her hands

steps: the letter at the same table

sequences.narration: Now the losses rise from the bottom. The lowest layer is wiped out first, then the next. The senior layer is still being paid, but its rating is cut, and its market value falls. In the real crisis, many senior securities lost money too.
sequences.understand: missing payments shrink the flow and losses climb from the bottom tranche up; senior pieces are hit last but fall in value

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: routes go grey and a value bar drops (P12)
concepts.why: it implies every investor lost the same way at once, which is inaccurate

concepts.name: the flood
concepts.idea: the pipe's flow thins; red rises from the foundation through equity into mezzanine; senior floors stay dry but their lights dim and they are marked 'downgraded'
concepts.why: loss allocation in its true order, in the same building, with their house among the red ones

accuracy: Losses hit the most junior tranche first and reach senior tranches only when they exceed the subordination below.
Do not show the senior floors destroyed by the first missed payments: in 2007–08 most senior pieces were downgraded and fell in market value, and losses came later and unevenly.
'Collapse' in the narration is shown as market value and ratings collapsing (overlay), not every floor flooding.

The narration says the example is simplified and that in the real crisis many senior securities lost money too; the senior floors staying dry is the example's subordination at work, not a claim about every senior security.
sequences.human_anchor: their house, now red in the foundation

transitions.motive: the camera sinks into the flooded foundation, then cuts to the kitchen table (match on the red)

storyboard.shows: losses rise from the bottom; senior dry but downgraded

steps: senior still paid, rating cut, value falls

sequences.narration: In September 2008, Lehman Brothers, heavily invested in mortgage-related assets, files for bankruptcy.
sequences.understand: the losses reached the largest institutions
sequences.feel: the scale of the consequence, felt at one table

concepts.name: literal baseline
concepts.idea: a newspaper front page on a desk (P12)
concepts.why: right document, wrong place: it floated free of the story

concepts.name: the newspaper on their table
concepts.idea: the (labelled, reconstructed) front page lies on the kitchen table beside her letter; push in on 'bankruptcy'
concepts.why: Wall Street's collapse and the family's notice in one frame: the through-line ends where it began

accuracy: Lehman filed on 15 September 2008; the front page is labelled an illustrative reconstruction, dated 16 September.

transitions.motive: hold on the two papers; the lamp by the sink is the last light
